paragraphs: OFG is a financial holding company headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico. OFG is subject to the provisions of the U.S. Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, (the "BHC Act") and accordingly, subject to the supervision and regulation of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "Federal Reserve Board"). OFG's principal subsidiary is Oriental Bank (the "Bank"), a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") insured Puerto Rico commercial bank founded as a federal savings and loan in 1964.

OFG provides comprehensive banking and financial services and solutions to its clients through the Bank and various other subsidiaries, including commercial, consumer, auto, and mortgage lending, financial planning, insurance sales, investment advisory and security brokerage services, as well as corporate trust services. OFG operates through three major business segments: Banking, Wealth Management, and Treasury. OFG provides most of its products and services to clients in Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands (the "USVI") and certain loan products in the continental United States. OFG operates through various subsidiaries, including a commercial bank, the Bank, a securities broker-dealer and investment adviser, Oriental Financial Services LLC ("Oriental Financial Services"), an insurance agency, Oriental Insurance, LLC ("Oriental Insurance"), a captive reinsurance company, OFG Reinsurance Ltd ("OFG Reinsurance"), OFG Ventures LLC ("OFG Ventures"), which holds investments, a commercial lender, OFG USA LLC ("OFG USA"), which is a subsidiary of the Bank, and OBPEF LLC ("OBPEF"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank and a private equity fund under the Puerto Rico Incentives Code, as amended (the "Incentives Code"), whose objective is to provide financing to eligible borrowers, whether in the form of senior or subordinated debt, to support the economic development of Puerto Rico. Most of our subsidiaries are based in San Juan, Puerto Rico and the USVI, except for OFG USA which is organized in Delaware, but operates out of Charlotte, North Carolina, OFG Reinsurance which is based in the Cayman Islands, and OFG Ventures which is based on Delaware.

OFG's mission is to make possible the progress of our customers, employees, shareholders, and communities we serve. As the world evolves rapidly, we seek to amplify our ambition, with the goal of advancing from steady progress to bold transformation. We believe that our strategy is designed to accelerate our transformation into a fully digital, data-driven, customer-centric financial institution, while maintaining the strong human relationships that define our brand. OFG aims to deliver intelligent growth, operational excellence, and deeper financial empowerment to make progress possible for our communities. Our strategy aspires to position OFG as a trusted digital financial coach, by understanding the customers' objectives and needs by offering value-added services that help them achieve financial progress and well-being. OFG is transitioning from a digital-first model to a truly digital bank, one where customers should be able to perform every financial activity seamlessly, securely, and intuitively, anytime, anywhere. Our goal is to provide a one-stop digital experience that is enriched by human connection and powered by intelligence. Our strategy is anchored on four main pillars:

•Customer Insights & Personalization: To enhance customer engagement, improve decision making and drive sustainable growth, with a unified, 360-degree view of the customer leverage on advance analytics to understand financial behaviors, patterns and lifecycle events to generate actionable customer insights that support the customer needs.
•Human Connection: Empower people by helping them to have smarter conversations while building trust and guiding customers through their most important financial decisions.

•Digital Bank: Become a truly digital bank, one where customers can do everything they would in a branch. The bank is no longer a place, but an experience that lives in their pockets, always ready, always personal, and better than ever.

•Business Excellence: OFG drives operational excellence through an agile operating model that is deeply embedded in our business and culture. We understand the customer's journey and align our structure and processes to reflect its perspective, end to end.

OFG's principal funding source is customer deposits. Through its branch network and digital sales platform, the Bank offers personal non-interest and interest-bearing checking accounts, savings accounts, certificates of deposit, individual retirement accounts ("IRAs") and commercial non-interest and interest-bearing checking accounts. The FDIC insures the Bank's deposit accounts up to applicable limits. Management makes retail deposit pricing decisions periodically, adjusting the rates paid on retail deposits in response to general market conditions and local competition. Pricing decisions take into account the rates being offered by other local banks, the applicable market benchmarks, and mainland U.S. market interest rates.

OFG has three reportable segments: Banking, Wealth Management, and Treasury. Management established the reportable segments based on the internal reporting used to evaluate performance and to assess where to allocate resources. Other factors such as OFG's organizational structure, nature of products, distribution channels and economic characteristics of the products or services were also considered in the determination of the reportable segments. OFG measures the performance of these reportable segments based on pre-established annual goals involving different financial parameters such as net income.
For detailed information regarding the performance of OFG's operating segments, please refer to "Note 28 – Business Segments" in OFG's accompanying consolidated financial statements.

The Bank, OFG's main subsidiary, is a full-service Puerto Rico commercial bank with its main office located in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Bank has 42 branches throughout Puerto Rico and 2 branches in the USVI. As an FDIC-insured Puerto Rico-chartered commercial bank, it is subject to examination by the FDIC and the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions of Puerto Rico (the "OCFI"). The Bank offers banking services such as commercial, consumer, auto, and mortgage lending, savings and time deposit products, and corporate trust services, and capitalizes on its retail banking network to provide commercial and mortgage lending products to its clients. The Bank has a wholly owned operating subsidiary, OFG USA, which is organized in Delaware but operates out of Charlotte, North Carolina. It also has two international banking entities (each an "IBE") organized in Puerto Rico pursuant to the International Banking Center Regulatory Act of Puerto Rico, as amended (the "IBE Act"), one of which is a unit operating within the Bank, named Oriental Overseas (the "IBE Unit"), and the other is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank, named Oriental International Bank, Inc. ("OIB" or the "IBE Subsidiary"). The IBE Unit and the IBE Subsidiary offer the Bank certain Puerto Rico tax advantages, and their services are limited under Puerto Rico law to persons and assets/liabilities located outside of Puerto Rico. In addition, the Bank has a wholly owned subsidiary, OBPEF, which is a private equity fund under the Incentives Code whose objective is to provide financing to eligible borrowers, whether in the form of senior or subordinated debt, to support the economic development of Puerto Rico.

Banking activities include the Bank's branches and mortgage banking activities with traditional retail banking products such as deposits, commercial loans, consumer loans, auto loans, and mortgage loans. The Bank's lending activities are primarily with customers located in Puerto Rico and the USVI. The Bank's lending transactions include a diversified number of industries and activities, all of which are encompassed within four main categories: commercial, consumer, mortgage and auto loans.

OFG's mortgage banking activities are conducted through a division of the Bank. The mortgage banking activities include the origination of mortgage loans for the Bank's own portfolio, the sale of loans directly into the secondary market or the securitization of mortgage loans into mortgage-backed securities, and the purchase or assumption of the right to service loans originated by others. The Bank originates Federal Housing Administration ("FHA") insured mortgages, Veterans Administration ("VA") guaranteed mortgages, and U.S. Department of Agriculture ("USDA") Rural Housing Service ("RHS") guaranteed loans that are primarily securitized for issuance of Government National Mortgage Association ("GNMA") mortgage-backed securities which can be resold to individual or institutional investors in the secondary market. Conventional loans that meet the underwriting requirements for sale or exchange under standard Federal National Mortgage Association (the "FNMA") or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (the "FHLMC") programs are referred to as conforming mortgage loans and are also securitized for issuance of FNMA or FHLMC mortgage-backed securities or sold through the Government Sponsor Entity ("GSE") cash window. The Bank is an approved seller of FNMA conforming mortgage loans for issuance of FNMA mortgage-backed securities. The Bank is also an approved issuer of GNMA mortgage-backed securities. The Bank is the master servicer of its mortgage loan portfolio and the GNMA, FNMA and FHLMC pools that it issues or services.

Auto loans: OFG provides financing for the purchase of new or used motor vehicles. These loans are generated mainly through dealers authorized and approved by OFG's auto credit department. The auto credit department has the specialized structure and resources to provide the service required for this product according to market demands and trends. The auto loan credit policy establishes specific guidance and parameters for the underwriting and origination processes. Underwriting procedures, lending limits, interest rate approval, insurance coverage, Fair Isaac Corporation ("FICO") score, and automobile brand restrictions are some parameters and internal controls implemented to ensure the quality and profitability of the auto loan portfolio. The proprietary credit scoring system is a fundamental part of the decision process.

paragraphs: In addition to other information set forth in this annual report on Form 10-K, you should carefully consider the following risk factors, as updated by other filings OFG makes with the SEC under the Exchange Act. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us at this time or that OFG currently deems immaterial may also adversely affect OFG's business, financial condition or results of operations.

Our business is directly affected by economic conditions within Puerto Rico. A significant portion of our credit risk exposure on our loan portfolio is concentrated in Puerto Rico. Thus, our profitability and financial condition may be adversely affected by an extended economic recession, adverse political, fiscal or economic developments in Puerto Rico, all of which could result in a reduction in loan originations, an increase in credit losses and a reduction in the value of our loans and loan servicing portfolio.

In the past, Puerto Rico has experienced significant economic contraction that persisted over a decade, a government fiscal crisis that led to the appointment of a federal oversight board in 2016 and a bankruptcy-type restructuring process of the government's finances. While Puerto Rico's economy has been gradually recovering, it still faces economic and fiscal challenges and could face additional economic or fiscal challenges in the future. Deterioration in local economic conditions or

in the financial condition of an industry on which the local market depends could adversely affect factors such as unemployment rates and real estate vacancy and values. This could result in, among other things, a reduction of creditworthy borrowers seeking loans, an increase in loan delinquencies, defaults and foreclosures, an increase in classified and non-accrual loans, a decrease in the value of collateral for loans, and a decrease in core deposits. Any of these factors could materially impact our business. In addition, there is no assurance that the Puerto Rico government will be able to satisfy its obligations as restructured.

Puerto Rico and the USVI are susceptible to earthquakes, hurricanes and major storms, the severity of which could be heightened by the effect of climate change, which could further deteriorate their economy and infrastructure.

Our branch network and business are concentrated in Puerto Rico and the USVI, which are susceptible to earthquakes, hurricanes and major storms that affect the local economy and the demand for our loans and financial services, as well as the ability of our customers to repay their loans. Any such natural disasters may further adversely affect Puerto Rico's and the USVI's infrastructure, which are generally weak and necessitating capital investment. This makes us vulnerable to downturns in Puerto Rico's and the USVI's economy as a result of natural disasters, the severity of which could increase as a result of the effects of climate change. Any subsequent earthquakes, hurricanes, major storms or other natural disasters could negatively affect or disrupt our operations and customer base and materially impact our business.

We have omitted discussion of 2023 results where it would be redundant to the discussion previously included in Item 7 of our 2024 annual report on Form 10-K. For our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, see Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our 2024 annual report on Form 10-K.

In January 2025, OFG announced that its Board of Directors (the "Board") approved the increase of its regular quarterly cash dividend to $0.30 per common share from $0.25 per share, beginning in the quarter ended March 31, 2025. In April 2025, the Board approved a new $100 million stock repurchase program. This new, open-ended program is in addition to the $50 million stock repurchase program approved by the Board in October 2024 (collectively, the "Existing Repurchase Programs"). Under the Existing Repurchase Programs, OFG repurchased 2,253,819 shares during 2025 for a total of $91.6 million at an average price of $40.64 per share. At December 31, 2025, the estimated remaining amount that may be purchased under the Existing Repurchase Programs is $38.1 million.
Announcement of Forthcoming 2026 Capital Actions

In January 2026, OFG announced that its Board approved the increase of its regular quarterly cash dividend to $0.35 per common share from $0.30 per share, beginning in the quarter ending March 31, 2026. The Board also approved a new $200 million stock repurchase program. This new, open-ended program is in addition to the Existing Repurchase Programs.

Puerto Rico's economy has continued to show stable performance, supported by favorable labor market conditions and adequate system liquidity. According to the Puerto Rico Department of Economic Development and Commerce, the Puerto Rico Economic Activity Index stood at 128.1 points in November 2025, representing a 0.8% increase compared to November 2024 and a consistent upward month-to-month trend in recent periods. Employment data published by such government agency

indicates continued gains across multiple industries. As of November 2025, total non-farm payroll employment averaged approximately 963,400 jobs, reflecting a 0.2% increase from the prior month and a 0.9% increase year over year. Economic activity has benefited from public sector reconstruction funding, private investment, and on-shoring initiatives. However, OFG continues to monitor global economic conditions, related uncertainties and their possible impact on Puerto Rico's economy, which could influence OFG's business and operational results.
CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES

The accounting and reporting policies followed by OFG conform with GAAP and general practices within the financial services industry. The preparation of these financial statements requires our management to make judgments, assumptions and estimates that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities. We evaluate these judgments, assumptions and estimates for changes that would affect the reported amounts. These estimates are based on management's historical industry experience and on various other judgments and assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results may differ from these judgments, assumptions and estimates. The following critical accounting estimate involves significant estimation uncertainty that has or is reasonably likely to have a material impact on our financial condition or results of operations. A discussion of OFG's significant accounting policies, including further discussion of the accounting estimate described below, can be found in "Note 1– Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" to the consolidated financial statements and should be read in conjunction with this section.

The most critical and complex accounting estimate is associated with the determination of the ACL. The provision for credit losses charged to current operations is based on this determination. The ACL represents management's best estimate deemed appropriate to provide current expected future credit losses in the portfolio as of the date of the reporting period.

OFG's management evaluates the adequacy of the ACL on a quarterly basis following a systematic methodology in order to provide for inherent risks in the loan portfolio. In developing its assessment of the adequacy of the ACL, OFG must rely on estimates and exercise judgment regarding matters where the ultimate outcome is unknown, such as economic developments affecting specific customers, industries or markets. Other factors that can affect management's estimates are the key drivers used for each macroeconomic scenario, the macroeconomic scenarios selected, and the weighting given to each scenario, among others. Significant changes in the financial condition of individual borrowers, in economic conditions, in historical loss experience, and in the condition of the various markets in which collateral may be sold may all affect the required level of the ACL. Consequently, the business, financial condition, liquidity, capital and results of operations could also be affected.

The ACL estimation requires management to use relevant forward-looking economic forecasts, by using variables such as employment and unemployment rate, gross national product ("GNP"), retail sales, and house price index, including in the application of reasonable and supportable forecasts. ACL estimations are performed by aggregating loans with similar risk characteristics.

OFG applied a discounted cash flow ("DCF") method for non-purchased credit deteriorated loans ("non-PCD") and an undiscounted cash flow ("UDCF") method for purchased credit deteriorated ("PCD") loans to determine the ACL for loans collectively measured for impairment, except for credit cards and overdrafts which utilize a remaining life methodology. For non-PCD, the expected cash flows are calculated for each loan and discounted using the effective yield. The discounted amount of expected cash flows is compared to the amortized cost, and any shortfall is recorded as a reserve. For PCD loans, the expected cash flows are calculated for each loan pool, pool reserve is calculated by aggregating total loss from the UDCF. Expected cash flows are resulted from applying the probability of default ("PD"), loss given default ("LGD"), and exposure at default ("EAD"). For the EAD, OFG uses a prepayment model that projects prepayments over the life of the loans.

Management's judgment is required in selecting the macroeconomic scenarios and the weighting of the economic scenarios, which consist of baseline and moderate recession scenarios. As of December 31, 2025, management gave more weight to the baseline scenario, except for the US loan segment where the moderate recession scenario was given a greater weight. Management selects the macroeconomic forecast that is most reflective of expectations at that point in time. The applicability of qualitative adjustments includes adjustments of inherent risk not captured by the quantitative model.

paragraphs: OFG 為一家財務控股公司，總部設於波多黎各聖胡安市。OFG 遵守美國 1956 年銀行控股公司法案（"BHC Act"）及其修正條文，並因此接受美國聯邦儲備系統理事會（"Federal Reserve Board"）的監督與管理。OFG 的主要子公司為東方銀行（"Bank"），為一家由美國儲蓄貸款協會轉型而來的波多黎各商業銀行，並受美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）保險，成立於 1964 年。

OFG 透過東方銀行及其他子公司，為客戶提供全面的銀行與財務服務與解決方案，包括商業貸款、消費貸款、汽車貸款、房貸、財務規劃、保險銷售、投資顧問及證券經紀服務，以及企業信託服務。OFG 透過三個主要業務分部運作：銀行、資產管理與財富管理、以及財務部。OFG 多數產品與服務提供給客戶於波多黎各與美國維珍羣島（"USVI"），並提供部分貸款產品於美國本土。OFG 透過多個子公司運作，包括一家商業銀行（Bank）、一家證券經紀與投資顧問公司（Oriental Financial Services LLC（"Oriental Financial Services"））、一家保險經紀公司（Oriental Insurance, LLC（"Oriental Insurance"））、一家自設再保險公司（OFG Reinsurance Ltd（"OFG Reinsurance"））、一家投資控股公司（OFG Ventures LLC（"OFG Ventures"））、一家商業貸款公司（OFG USA LLC（"OFG USA"）），為 Bank 之子公司，以及 OBPEF LLC（"OBPEF"），為 Bank 之全資子公司，並為波多黎各鼓勵條例（"Incentives Code"）修正後之私人股權基金，其目標為提供符合資格借款人之融資，無論為優先或次級債務，以支持波多黎各之經濟發展。我們多數子公司設於聖胡安市、波多黎各與 USVI，唯 OFG USA 為設於特拉華州，但營運於北卡羅萊納州夏洛特市，OFG Reinsurance 為設於開曼羣島，OFG Ventures 則設於特拉華州。

OFG 的使命為協助我們服務的客戶、員工、股東與社區實現進步。隨著世界快速演進，我們追求提升抱負，目標為從穩定進步轉向大膽轉型。我們相信，我們的策略設計可加速轉型為一家完全數位化、數據驅動、以客戶為中心的金融機構，同時維持我們品牌所代表的強大人際關係。OFG 的目標為實現智能成長、運營卓越與更深層的財務賦能，以實現社區的進步。我們的策略旨在將 OFG 定位為受信賴的數位財務顧問，透過瞭解客戶的目標與需求，提供附加價值服務，協助他們實現財務進步與福祉。OFG 正從以數位為先的模式轉型為一家真正數位銀行，讓客戶能在任何時間、任何地點，順暢、安全且直覺地執行所有金融活動。我們的目標是提供一個一站式數位體驗，並透過人際連結與智慧驅動來豐富此體驗。我們的策略以四大支柱為基礎：
•客戶洞察與個人化：為提升客戶參與度、改善決策並推動可持續成長，透過統一的 360 度客戶視角，運用先進分析技術，瞭解客戶的財務行為、模式與生命週期事件，以產生可行動的客戶洞察，支持客戶需求。
•人際連結：透過協助人們進行更智慧的對話，建立信任，並引導客戶做出最重要的財務決策。
•數位銀行：成為一家真正數位銀行，讓客戶能執行所有在分行內進行的金融活動。銀行不再是一個場所，而是一種體驗，隨時隨地為客戶準備好，並更具個人化與優越性。
•業務卓越：OFG 透過敏捷的運營模式推動運營卓越，此模式深植於我們的業務與文化中。我們瞭解客戶的旅程，並調整我們的組織與流程以反映其視角，從頭至尾。
OFG 的主要資金來源為客戶存款。透過其分行網路與數位銷售平台，銀行提供個人非利息與利息產生的支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶、存款憑證、個人退休帳戶（"IRAs"）與商業非利息與利息產生的支票帳戶。FDIC 保險銀行的存款帳戶至適用的保險上限。管理層定期做出零售存款利率決策，根據總體市場條件與當地競爭情況調整零售存款利率。利率決策考量其他本地銀行提供的利率、適用的市場指標與美國本土市場利率。
OFG 有三個應報告分部：銀行、資產管理與證券投資信託，以及財務部門。管理階層根據內部用以評估績效及決定資源配置的報表，設立了這些應報告分部。其他因素，例如 OFG 的組織架構、產品性質、通路管道及產品或服務的經濟特性，也在決定應報告分部時被考慮。OFG 依據預先設定的年度目標，以不同財務參數（如淨收入）來衡量這些應報告分部的績效。
如需詳細資訊關於 OFG 操作分部的績效，請參閱 OFG 附屬財務報表中的「附註 28 – 商業分部」。

銀行為 OFG 的主要子公司，為一家在波多黎各設立、提供全方位服務的商業銀行，總部設於波多黎各聖胡安。銀行在波多黎各設有 42 家分行，並在美國維京羣島設有 2 家分行。作為一家受美國存款保險公司（FDIC） insure 的波多黎各註冊商業銀行，其需接受 FDIC 與波多黎各金融機構委員會（OCFI）的監督。銀行提供商業、消費、汽車及房貸貸款、儲蓄與定期存款產品，以及企業信託服務，並透過其零售銀行網路為客戶提供商業與房貸貸款產品。銀行設有 wholly owned 的營運子公司 OFG USA，於德克薩斯州夏洛特市營運，其設立於特拉華州。銀行亦設有兩家國際銀行機構（每家為一「國際銀行機構」，簡稱 IBE），依據波多黎各國際銀行中心規範法案（IBE Act）設立，其中一家為銀行內設的單位，名為 Oriental Overseas（IBE Unit），另一家為銀行的 wholly owned 子公司，名為 Oriental International Bank, Inc.（OIB 或 IBE 子公司）。IBE Unit 與 IBE 子公司為銀行提供某些波多黎各稅務優勢，其服務根據波多黎各法律僅限於位於波多黎各以外的個人與資產/負債。此外，銀行設有 wholly owned 子公司 OBPEF，為根據波多黎各鼓勵投資法設立的私人股權基金，其目標為為符合資格的借款人提供融資，無論是以高級或次級債務形式，以支持波多黎各的經濟發展。
銀行業務包括銀行的分行與房貸銀行業務，以及傳統零售銀行產品，如存款、商業貸款、消費貸款、汽車貸款與房貸貸款。銀行的貸款業務主要針對位於波多黎各與美國維京羣島的客戶。銀行的貸款交易涵蓋多樣化的產業與活動，皆歸納於四個主要類別：商業貸款、消費貸款、房貸貸款與汽車貸款。

OFG 的房貸銀行業務透過銀行的部門進行。房貸銀行業務包括為銀行自有資產組合發放房貸、直接銷售貸款至次級市場或將房貸證券化為房貸支持證券，以及購買或承購由他人發放貸款的服務權。銀行發放美國住房管理局（FHA） insure 的房貸、退伍軍人管理局（VA） guarantee 的房貸，以及美國農業部鄉村住宅服務（RHS） guarantee 的貸款，這些貸款主要證券化為政府國家房貸協會（GNMA）房貸支持證券，可再出售至個人或機構投資者在次級市場。符合標準美國住宅抵押貸款協會（FNMA）或美國住宅貸款抵押銀行（FHLMC）程式銷售或交換條件的貸款稱為符合標準的房貸，亦可證券化為 FNMA 或 FHLMC 的房貸支持證券，或透過政府支持機構（GSE）現金窗口銷售。銀行為 FNMA 合規房貸的批准銷售方，用以發行 FNMA 房貸支持證券。銀行亦為 GNMA 房貸支持證券的批准發行方。銀行為其房貸貸款組合及發行或服務的 GNMA、FNMA 與 FHLMC 池的主服務機構。

汽車貸款：OFG 提供購買新或二手機動車的融資。這些貸款主要透過經 OFG 汽車信貸部門核准與授權的經銷商產生。汽車信貸部門擁有專門的結構與資源，以根據市場需求與趨勢提供此產品所需的服務。汽車貸款信貸政策設定了針對貸款評估與發放程序的特定指引與參數。貸款評估程序、貸款上限、利率批准、保險覆蓋範圍、公平信用評分機構（FICO）分數與汽車品牌限制為部分參數與內部控制措施，以確保汽車貸款組合的品質與獲利性。專屬信貸評分系統為貸款決策過程中的基本組成部分。

2025 年 1 月，OFG 宣佈其董事會（「董事會」）批准將其定期季度現金股息提高至每普通股 0.30 美元，自 2025 年 3 月 31 日結息季度起生效，由原來每普通股 0.25 美元。2025 年 4 月，董事會批准了一項新的 100 百萬美元股票買回計畫。此新、開放式計畫為 2024 年 10 月董事會批准的 50 百萬美元股票買回計畫（合稱「現有買回計畫」）之外的額外計畫。根據現有買回計畫，OFG 在 2025 年買回 2,253,819 股，總計 91.6 百萬美元，平均每股 40.64 美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，根據現有買回計畫，預計可買回的剩餘金額為 38.1 百萬美元。
2026 年財務行動預告
2026 年 1 月，OFG 宣佈其董事會批准將其定期季度現金股息提高至每普通股 0.35 美元，自 2026 年 3 月 31 日結息季度起生效，由原來每普通股 0.30 美元。董事會同時批准了一項新的 200 百萬美元股票買回計畫。此新、開放式計畫為現有買回計畫之外的額外計畫。
波多黎各經濟持續顯示穩定表現，受益於有利的勞動市場條件及充足的系統流動性。根據波多黎各經濟發展與貿易部資料，波多黎各經濟活動指數在2025年11月為128.1點，較2024年11月成長0.8%，並在近期期間顯示一致的月增趨勢。該政府機構發布的就業資料
顯示多個產業持續增加。截至2025年11月，總非農業薪資就業平均約為963,400個職位，反映較前一月成長0.2%，且年增成長0.9%。經濟活動受益於公部門重建資金、私人投資及在岸化措施。然而，OFG持續監測全球經濟條件、相關不確定性及其可能對波多黎各經濟的影響，這些因素可能影響OFG的業務與營運結果。
關鍵會計政策與會計估計

OFG遵循的會計與報導政策符合GAAP及金融服務業的一般慣例。這些財務報表的編製需要我們管理階層做出判斷、假設與估計，這些會影響資產、負債、收入與費用的報導數字，以及相關的或有資產與負債揭露。我們評估這些判斷、假設與估計是否會影響報導數字。這些估計基於管理階層的歷史產業經驗，以及在特定情況下認為合理的其他判斷與假設。實際結果可能與這些判斷、假設與估計不同。以下關鍵會計估計涉及重大估計不確定性，這些估計可能或合理可能對我們的財務狀況或營運結果產生重大影響。有關OFG的重要會計政策討論，包括以下會計估計的進一步說明，可參閱「附註1–重要會計政策摘要」至合併財務報表，並應與本節一併閱讀。
最關鍵且複雜的會計估計與應計壞帳準備金（ACL）的確定有關。針對現行營運所計提的信用損失準備金，係根據此一確定結果。ACL 代表管理階層認為適當的預估數值，用以反映截至財務報導期間截止日，資產組閤中預期未來的信用損失。

OFG 管理階層每季評估 ACL 是否充足，並依照系統化的方法，以反映貸款組閤中固有的風險。在評估 ACL 是否充足時，OFG 必須依賴估計數值，並對一些最終結果未知的項目行使判斷，例如影響特定客戶、產業或市場的經濟發展。其他可能影響管理階層估計數值的因素，包括每種總體經濟情境所使用的關鍵變數、所選取的總體經濟情境，以及每種情境所給予的權重，等等。個別借款人的財務狀況、經濟條件、歷史損失經驗，以及擔保品可能出售之各市場狀況的重大變動，均可能影響所需 ACL 的水準。因此，公司的營運、財務狀況、流動性、資本及營運成果也可能受到影響。
ACL 的估計需要管理階層使用相關的前瞻性經濟預測，並使用如就業率與失業率、國民所得總額（"GNP"）、零售銷售額及住宅價格指數等變數，包括在合理且可支持的預測應用中。ACL 的估計係透過將具有類似風險特徵的貸款進行歸類後進行計算。

OFG 對非購入信用惡化貸款（"非 PCD"）採用折現現金流（"DCF"）法，對購入信用惡化貸款（"PCD"）則採用未折現現金流（"UDCF"）法，以確定 collectively measured for impairment 的貸款之 ACL，除了信用卡及透支貸款，這些貸款則採用剩餘使用年限法。對於非 PCD，每筆貸款的預期現金流會進行計算，並以有效收益率折現。預期現金流的折現金額與攤銷成本進行比較，任何差額會計入準備金。對於 PCD 貸款，每筆貸款組的預期現金流會進行計算，組別準備金則透過將 UDCF 的總損失進行歸類計算。預期現金流係透過應用違約機率（"PD"）、違約損失（"LGD"）及違約時之風險敞口（"EAD"）計算得出。對於 EAD，OFG 會使用預付款模型，以預測貸款壽命期間的預付款情況。
在選擇總體經濟情境及經濟情境權重時，需要管理階層的判斷，這些情境包括基準情境與溫和衰退情境。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，管理階層對基準情境給予較高權重，除了美國貸款分部，該分部對溫和衰退情境給予較高權重。管理階層會選擇最反映當時預期的總體經濟預測。品質調整的適用性包括對量化模型未涵蓋的內在風險進行調整。
OFG 的敏感度分析並不代表管理階層對 2025 年 12 月 31 日預期信用損失的觀點。OFG 透過對基準與溫和衰退情境給予 100% 的權重來評估敏感度。對於給予 100%

headings: 本公司大多數業務是在波多黎各進行，當地的總體經濟與政府財政及流動性挑戰已對我們造成不利影響，並可能持續造成不利影響。
波多黎各依賴聯邦災難救濟資金，若這些資金發放延宕，可能對當地經濟造成不利影響。
政治變動可能帶來的不利影響，可能幹擾波多黎各的經濟復甦過程。
聯邦貿易政策的不利變化以及聯邦緊急與刺激資金逐步減少，可能影響我們的業務與股票價格。
利率變動可能對OFG的營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
信用風險增加可能導致我們必須提高信用損失提列準備金，這可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
我們在房貸貸款發放方面面臨違約及其他風險。
房地產市場走跌可能導致違約、違約及法拍案件增加，以及貸款發放活動減少，這將對我們的財務結果造成不利影響。
全球性軍事衝突可能影響我們所有業務運作、收入、成本及股票價格。
我們可能因詐欺及竊盜而遭受損失。
我們因使用科技而面臨安全及運營風險，包括遭受網路攻擊或網路竊盜的風險。
未遵守美國 patriot 法案、銀行保密法或其他法律及法規，可能會導致處罰及其他制裁。
若我們無法維持或增加核心存款，我們可能面臨支付更高資金成本，且淨利息收入可能減少。
消費者保護法規可能降低我們的非利息收入。
我們的風險管理政策、程序及系統可能不足以緩解各項業務內在的風險。
金融服務業的不利發展可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司業務若無法維持取得穩定資金來源，可能會受到不利影響。
本公司自子公司取得股息的能力，可能影響本公司流動性及支付股息給股東的能力。
若無法跟上科技變革的腳步，包括人工智慧的發展，可能會對OFG的營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
與其他金融機構的競爭可能會對本公司利潤率造成不利影響。
本公司營運於高度管制的產業，可能因聯邦及地方法規的變動而受到不利影響。
聲譽風險及社會因素可能影響本公司結果。
本公司採用人工智慧技術，可能面臨不斷演進的法律、法規及營運風險。
財務會計準則委員會（"FASB"）或其他標準制定機構所頒布的會計準則變動，可能會對本公司財務報表造成不利影響。

paragraphs: 除本年度報告書（Form 10-K）中所載之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列風險因素，並注意 OFG 會根據證券交易法（Exchange Act）向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交之其他申報文件所更新之內容。目前尚有其他風險與不確定性，我們尚未知悉或 OFG 目前認為不重要，這些因素也可能對 OFG 之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成不利影響。
我們之業務直接受波多黎各總體經濟狀況之影響。我們貸款組閤中之信用風險敞口有相當大一部分集中於波多黎各。因此，若波多黎各發生長期經濟衰退，或該地政治、財政或經濟出現不利發展，可能對我們之獲利能力與財務狀況造成不利影響，這可能會導致貸款發放減少、信用損失增加，以及我們貸款與貸款服務組合之價值下降。
過去，波多黎各曾經歷持續十年之顯著經濟衰退，並引發財政危機，導致 2016 年設立聯邦監督委員會，以及政府財務進行類似破產之重整程序。雖然波多黎各經濟已逐漸復甦，但該地仍面臨經濟與財政挑戰，未來亦可能面臨更多經濟或財政挑戰。當地經濟條件惡化或
依賴之產業財務狀況惡化，可能會對失業率、不動產空置率與價值等要素造成不利影響。這可能會導致，例如信用良好之借款人尋求貸款減少、貸款逾期與違約與法拍增加、分類與未計息貸款增加、貸款擔保品價值下降，以及核心存款減少。任何這些因素都可能對我們之業務造成重大影響。此外，無法保證波多黎各政府能履行其重整後之義務。
波多黎各與美屬維京羣島（USVI）易受地震、颶風與重大風暴影響，其嚴重程度可能因氣候變遷之影響而增加，這可能會進一步惡化其經濟與基礎建設。

我們之分行網路與業務集中於波多黎各與美屬維京羣島，這些地區易受地震、颶風與重大風暴影響，影響當地經濟與貸款與金融服務之需求，以及客戶償還貸款之能力。任何此類天然災害可能進一步對波多黎各與美屬維京羣島之基礎建設造成不利影響，而這些基礎建設通常較弱，需進行資本投資。這使我們對波多黎各與美屬維京羣島經濟衰退更加敏感，而此類天然災害之嚴重程度可能因氣候變遷之影響而增加。任何隨後發生之地震、颶風、重大風暴或其他天然災害都可能對我們之營運與客戶羣造成負面影響或幹擾，並對我們之業務造成重大影響。
